def: A small build that shows whether an idea can work at all, before anyone commits to making it reliable.
A limited trial with real users on real work for a fixed period, used to learn whether a system works in the customer's setting.
The state in which people rely on a system for their normal work, it keeps running unattended, and someone is accountable for it.
A named launch condition backed by evidence that an outsider can inspect, with a person who may say no.
Running a model on real inputs while humans keep deciding, recording its answers without showing or acting on them.
A sequence of rollout stages, from shadow to assist to partial and wider automation, each earned with evidence and reversible.
A unique identifier for an intended action, stored by the receiver so that a repeated request is recognised and not carried out twice.
A thin internal service or library through which all model calls pass, holding timeouts, spend caps, fallbacks and provider choice.
The work of helping the people affected by a new system adopt it, keep their trust calibrated and change how they work.
The tendency to accept an automated system's output without checking it, especially when the output is fluent.
